name: Oil (Brent)
summary: Brent near $90 on 20 Nov, 23% lower over a month; Hormuz attacks continue but a supply surplus weighs
state: Brent was near $90.1 early on 20 Nov, 2.6% lower on the week and 23% lower over a month, inside the $85–110 Watch band and 24% below its 52-week high of $118 (Yahoo Finance). Prices were heading for a third weekly fall on 20 Nov as the IEA projected a global surplus of about 2 mb/d this quarter, offsetting concern over possible renewed US strikes on Iran (Trading Economics). Tanker attacks around Hormuz continued on 16–18 Nov, but no new outage above 2 mb/d was confirmed.
for_you: Fuel and heating oil costs follow crude with a lag of weeks. Lower crude eases pressure on pump prices, but the Gulf conflict keeps the risk of sudden price jumps higher than usual for drivers, hauliers and airlines.
why: Oil feeds inflation, transport and household budgets; price spikes have preceded most post-war recessions.
drivers: OPEC+ output, Middle East supply risk, sanctions, demand, inventories, shipping disruption.

rubric.alert: Brent > $110, or 1-month change > +30%, or a major physical supply outage (> 2 mb/d).
